label: Early copy-phase steps (echoing original tokens 0-1) in length-9 sequences, token-gated
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never during the original phase or on the <DEL> step. It is concentrated on the first few copy steps (recall_idx 1-3, absolute t=10-12) and almost entirely in long sequences (L=9 holds 90% of mass, L=8 holds 9%, L<=6 essentially zero). In practice it fires when the model is fed back original tokens 0-2. Inside that window, whether it fires depends strongly on the identity of the echoed input token: v is the strongest (top examples are mostly v at the first copy input), followed by y, m, e, k, u. Many window steps with other tokens (s, p, b, d, a, l, ...) stay silent, so precision is low (~0.28). Out-of-copy and late-copy steps are almost never active (a small tail at the last two copy steps). Predicate captures ~80% of activation mass; no simple token rule raises F1 beyond ~0.40.
